neighbours.label: describing something as done quickly and without waste (brisk, swift, streamlined, efficient), or proposing the direct option with 'why not (just)'
fire: The nurse moved down the ward with a brisk step, checking each chart.
After lunch we kept up a brisk trot all the way to the harbour.
A swift decision by the board ended the dispute within days.
The airline now runs a streamlined boarding process at every gate.
Our accountant is an efficient woman who files everything by Friday.
If the printer jams every day, why not just buy another one?
You already have the keys, so why not drive there yourself tonight?
If the tent leaks that badly, why not just sleep in the car?
quiet: The nurse moved down the ward with a tired step, checking each chart.
After lunch we kept up a gentle stroll all the way to the harbour.
A delayed decision by the board dragged the dispute on for years.
The airline now runs a complicated boarding process at every gate.
Our accountant is a forgetful woman who loses everything by Friday.
If the printer jams every day, what should we tell the manager?
You already have the keys, so I will not drive there myself tonight.
The tent leaks that badly because nobody ever repaired the seams.

notes: Card peaks mix ' not'/' just' with ' efficient'/' brisk'. Probes: slow/long/careless counterparts stay near zero, plain 'not' stays near zero. Whether the shared pattern is real or two jobs is open; the test mixes both sides.
